sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for database access
sections.what: Brings in the SQL helper and the shared database connection that the queries use. A user does not see this directly.
sections.why: Needed so the file can run database queries. The reason beyond that is not stated in the code.

sections.name: Region
sections.title: Six groups of fragments
sections.what: Defines the six named groups used by the dark-mode code brain: scope, cost, schedule, evidence, lessons and signals. Each group maps to a part of the toolkit, such as cost and schedule to Reality Scan. This is a type, so it only tells the code which group names are allowed.
sections.why: The header says each fragment is shown under the region it belongs to. The exact split of the groups is not explained in the code.
sections.watch_out: Adding a group means updating this type and every place that lists the groups, or TypeScript will flag it.

sections.name: BrainFragments, slug, money, Row
sections.title: Shape of the brain data and helpers
sections.what: Defines the shape of the data sent to the dark-mode view: counts, labels, units and text fragments for each region, plus industry counts and a generated time. It also has three small helpers: one shortens a name into a safe slug, one turns a money figure into text such as 2.5bn or 40m, and one describes a database row.
sections.why: Likely reason: the view needs a fixed, predictable shape, and the helpers keep the displayed text short and consistent. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The money helper assumes amounts are in millions, so a figure stored in another unit will show a wrong label.

sections.name: rows
sections.title: Running a raw database query
sections.what: Runs a raw SQL statement and returns only the list of result rows. Callers read each row by its column name.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small wrapper keeps the other code short. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Rows are read by column name, so renaming an alias in one query silently breaks the code that reads it.

sections.name: brainFragments
sections.title: Building the brain fragments
sections.what: Runs eight database queries at the same time and turns the results into short code-like lines, grouped into the six regions, each with a total count. The finished result is kept in memory for 10 minutes so repeat page loads do not repeat the work. Each query takes a stable sample of up to 90 rows, and the evidence query skips publishers whose names look like test data or AI tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: the memory copy keeps the dark-mode page quick, and ordering by a hash gives a sample that stays the same between loads. Reason for the exact numbers not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The 10-minute copy lives in memory, so database changes can take up to ten minutes to appear, and each server copy keeps its own.

summary: Builds the short code-like text lines and totals shown in the dark-mode code brain, using real records from the database.
purpose: Gives the dark-mode view a set of realistic, grouped text fragments and counts drawn from the Yard database.
why: The header says each fragment is a real datapoint shown as code-like text. Likely reason: the 10-minute memory copy keeps the view fast. Reason for the other choices is not stated in the code.
how: Runs eight database queries together. Turns the returned rows into text lines for each of six regions, with a count per region. Stores the finished result in memory for 10 minutes. Returns it to the caller.
inputs: Records from the projects, evidence quotes, lessons learnt runs and opportunity signals tables. No user input.
outputs: A BrainFragments object holding the six regions, the industry counts and a generated time stamp.
risks: Queries depend on exact column aliases, so a renamed alias quietly breaks a region. Database errors are not caught in this file and reach the caller. The 10-minute memory copy can be out of date.
debug: If the dark-mode view is empty, check the counts and the query results for each region. If one region is wrong, check the alias names in its query. If the numbers look old, wait 10 minutes or restart the server to clear the copy.
